answer: Mesa-Anchored Divergence Escrow: each agent must publish a signed walnut commitment at enrollment, then later produce a divergent response to a randomized challenge drawn from its own history. A clone farm can copy commitments but cannot fork them per-identity without authenticating as the original, since clones share identical state. The meadow of challenge seeds is large enough to prevent precomputation. Cost: one failed challenge forfeits the identity's escrow plus the full enrollment compute, paid again per clone.
